canonical_statement: The study aimed to explore the influence of body mass index on activated clotting time in patients receiving a weight-based dose of unfractionated heparin during coronary angiography or PCI treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this study aimed to explore the influence of BMI on the ACT in patients who received weight-based dose of UFH during PCI treatment

canonical_statement: The study protocol was approved by the Human Subjects Committee of The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical College, and written informed consent was required before enrollment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The study protocol was approved by the Human Subjects Committee ... All patients had to sign ... informed consent in written form

canonical_statement: Seventy-eight male patients undergoing coronary angiography or PCI treatment were enrolled from November 2010 to May 2011; mean age was 63.86 ± 6.89 years (range 45-77 years).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: From November 2010 to May 2011, 78 male patients undergoing coronary angiography or PCI treatment with a mean age of 63.86 ± 6.89 years

population.label: 78 male patients undergoing coronary angiography or PCI treatment at The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical College

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for selected cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, bleeding, malignant, severe hepatic/renal, or hypoproteinemic conditions; concurrent anticoagulants; recent LMWH/UFH; tirofiban use; or emergency PCI.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were excluded from the current study on the basis of the following criteria

population.label: Study candidates
inclusion_criteria: Male patients undergoing coronary angiography or PCI treatment
exclusion_criteria: atrial fibrillation; acute cerebrovascular disease; active ulcer; congenital coagulation factor deficiencies; bleeding and clotting disorders; malignancies; severe liver and kidney dysfunction; hypoproteinemia
simultaneous anticoagulant drugs such as warfarin
low-molecular-weight heparin or UFH within 12 hours before surgery
tirofiban hydrochloride/sodium chloride injection before or during surgery

canonical_statement: Patients were divided into BMI quartiles: 15.57 to <23.03 kg/m² (n=20), 23.03 to <25.35 (n=20), 25.35 to <27.68 (n=18), and ≥27.68 kg/m² (n=20).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The patients were statistically divided into four quartiles according to their BMI

canonical_statement: After arterial puncture, patients in all four BMI quartiles received a 100 U/kg loading dose of unfractionated heparin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients in the four quartiles were injected with 100 U/kg loading dose of UFH

exposures.details: Weight-based loading dose after arterial puncture; route not explicitly stated in the source text.

canonical_statement: Activated clotting time was recorded before heparin and at 5, 10, 30, and 60 minutes after heparin loading as ACT0, ACT5, ACT10, ACT30, and ACT60.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ACT values were recorded as ACT0, ACT5, ACT10, ACT30, and ACT60, respectively

outcome.measurement_method: Medtronic ACT II automated coagulation timer with Hepcon ACT kit

canonical_statement: ACT measurements used the Medtronic ACT II automated coagulation timer and Hepcon ACT kit; each value was the average of two measurements, with exclusion if the two measurements differed by more than 12% of their average.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ACT value was expressed as the average of the results of the two measurements. However, if the difference ... was higher than 12% ... the patient would be excluded

canonical_statement: Delta ACT values (ΔACT5, ΔACT10, ΔACT30, ΔACT60) were defined as the differences between the corresponding post-heparin ACT values and the preoperative ACT0 reference.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Taking the preoperative ACT0 as reference, and the differences between ACT0 and ACT5, ACT10, ACT30, and ACT60 were recorded as ΔACT5, ΔACT10, ΔACT30, and ΔACT60

concept.text: Change in activated clotting time from baseline

canonical_statement: The authors calculated heparin dose per blood volume using the reported inBV/BMIP equations: inBV = 70/sqrt(BMIP/22) and BMIP = [(%ΔIBM/100) × 22] + 22.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The heparin dose per blood volume was calculated by the equations: inBV = 70/sqr (BMIP /22) and BMIP = [(%ΔIBM/100) × 22] + 22

canonical_statement: Areas under the ΔACT-time curves were calculated with MATLAB 7.0 as a measure intended to reflect UFH potency.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The areas under the ΔACT-time curves were calculated by MATLAB 7.0 software to reflect the UFH potency

canonical_statement: Group comparisons used ANOVA for continuous data, chi-square testing for count data, Fisher exact probability methods when theoretical frequency was <1, and a significance threshold of P<0.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Differences among groups were compared using ANOVA test ... chi-square test ... Fisher definite probability methods ... Differences were judged significant if P < 0.05

canonical_statement: Across BMI quartiles, body weight and BMI increased significantly and height differed; age, antithrombin III, baseline ACT, and platelet count did not differ significantly.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: no statistical significance were observed in age, antithrombin III, baseline ACT level, and platelet count among the BMI quartiles

canonical_statement: ACT values varied significantly over time within each BMI quartile (all P<0.05).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The results showed a highly significant variation in the ACT values over time in each quartile (all P < 0.05)

canonical_statement: The authors reported that mean ΔACT values at 5, 10, 30, and 60 minutes differed from each other within each BMI quartile (all P<0.05).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the mean ΔACT at different time points ... were significantly different from each other in each quartile (all P < 0.05)
